title: Bradley Walsh: Out of This World on Sky HISTORY tonight – time, channel and what to expect as he searches for the lost city of Atlantis
excerpt: Bradley Walsh: Out of This World airs tonight at 9pm on Sky HISTORY. Find out what happens as Bradley investigates Atlantis, UFOs and ancient mysteries.
content:
Bradley Walsh is heading on another extraordinary adventure tonight as he investigates some of the world’s greatest unexplained mysteries in Bradley Walsh: Out of This World, airing on Sky HISTORY at 9pm.

The popular television presenter and host of The Chase swaps the quiz studio for an international mystery-hunting expedition, as he attempts to answer one of the biggest questions in human history: are we really alone?

From UFO sightings and unexplained military encounters to ancient civilisations, underwater discoveries, Stonehenge and mysterious crop circles, Bradley travels across the world to examine evidence that could challenge what we think we know about our planet.

Tonight’s episode turns its attention to one of history’s most enduring mysteries – Atlantis. Bradley follows ancient clues from Gibraltar to the Spanish coast, investigating whether the legendary lost city could have been based on a real place hidden beneath the waves.

Armed with plenty of questions, his trademark humour and a healthy dose of scepticism, Bradley is determined to follow the evidence wherever it leads.

Here’s everything you need to know about Bradley Walsh: Out of This World, including what time it starts, which channel it is on and what viewers can expect from tonight’s Atlantis investigation.

Bradley Walsh: Out of This World airs tonight, Tuesday 17 November 2026, at 9pm on Sky HISTORY.

The programme is part of Bradley’s new four-part series exploring mysteries surrounding the unexplained, ancient history and the possibility of extraterrestrial life.

Tonight’s episode is titled Atlantis and has a running time of approximately 43 minutes.

What is Bradley Walsh: Out of This World about?

Bradley Walsh: Out of This World sees the presenter embark on a global journey to investigate some of the most fascinating and controversial mysteries in history.

The series explores questions that have captivated people for generations. Could there be intelligent life beyond Earth? Have military personnel witnessed unexplained flying objects? Was Atlantis a real civilisation? And what is behind the mysterious formations that regularly appear in British crop fields?

Rather than simply accepting extraordinary claims, Bradley meets eyewitnesses, researchers, historians and experts to hear their accounts and examine the evidence.

His approach combines curiosity with a healthy scepticism, making him an accessible guide for viewers who enjoy exploring unusual theories without necessarily believing everything they hear.

The series also benefits from Bradley’s natural sense of humour, ensuring that the investigations remain entertaining as well as thought-provoking.

From UFO encounters to underwater discoveries, there is no shortage of extraordinary claims to investigate.

Tonight’s episode: Bradley Walsh searches for Atlantis

Tonight’s episode focuses on Atlantis, the legendary lost city that has fascinated historians, archaeologists and explorers for centuries.

Bradley follows a trail of ancient clues from Gibraltar to the Spanish coastline, exploring whether the story of Atlantis could have been inspired by a real civilisation.

The investigation takes him into the world of ancient mythology, archaeological discoveries and underwater mysteries, as he attempts to separate historical evidence from speculation.

Atlantis has traditionally been associated with the writings of the ancient Greek philosopher Plato, who described a powerful civilisation that supposedly disappeared beneath the sea.

For centuries, people have attempted to identify where this lost civilisation might have existed. Suggested locations have ranged from the Mediterranean to the Atlantic, with numerous theories attempting to explain Plato’s account.

Bradley explores some of these ideas and meets people who believe they may have uncovered evidence pointing towards the Spanish coast.

Could the answer to one of history’s greatest mysteries really be hidden beneath the water?

Could Atlantis have been hidden beneath the waves off Spain?

One of the most intriguing aspects of tonight’s programme is the investigation into the waters around Spain.

Bradley follows ancient clues towards the area around Cádiz, where researchers have explored possible links between the landscape and Plato’s description of Atlantis.

The investigation considers historical accounts, archaeological finds and underwater evidence that could offer fresh insight into the mystery.

Sonar technology and underwater imaging also play a role in examining what may lie beneath the surface.

The challenge is determining whether unusual underwater formations are evidence of an ancient settlement or whether they have more ordinary geological explanations.

There is no universally accepted archaeological proof that Atlantis existed as a real city, but that has done little to diminish interest in the subject.

For Bradley, the appeal is in investigating the claims, listening to those who believe they have found something significant and deciding how convincing the evidence really is.

The result promises to be an intriguing journey through ancient history, mythology and underwater exploration.

What other mysteries does Bradley Walsh investigate?

Although Atlantis is the focus of tonight’s episode, the wider series covers several other extraordinary subjects.

Across the four episodes, Bradley investigates UFO sightings, unidentified submerged objects (USOs), military encounters, Stonehenge and crop circles.

UFO sightings and unexplained military encounters

The series examines reports of unexplained objects in the skies, including accounts from people with military backgrounds.

Bradley meets witnesses who describe extraordinary encounters and investigates why some sightings have continued to attract attention decades after they were first reported.

The programme also looks at historical cases and the information contained in previously classified or released documents.

Underwater mysteries and unidentified submerged objects

The investigation does not stop at the skies.

Bradley also explores reports of unidentified submerged objects, including mysterious discoveries beneath the Baltic Sea.

These unusual underwater formations have prompted speculation about possible spacecraft, ancient structures and unexplained natural phenomena.

The programme examines the evidence and considers what could really be responsible.

Stonehenge and the mystery of crop circles

Another part of the series takes Bradley to Wiltshire, where he investigates the enduring mysteries surrounding Stonehenge.

The prehistoric monument continues to attract questions about how it was constructed, why it was built and what role it played in ancient society.

Bradley also ventures into crop circle country to examine the strange patterns that have appeared in fields across the UK.

Are these formations the result of elaborate human activity, natural phenomena or something more unusual?

As always, the programme follows the evidence while leaving viewers to make up their own minds.

Why is Bradley Walsh presenting Out of This World?

Bradley Walsh has become one of Britain’s most recognisable television presenters, thanks to programmes including The Chase and a variety of entertainment and factual shows.

His enthusiasm, approachable personality and ability to connect with people make him a natural fit for a series built around asking questions and investigating unusual stories.

In Out of This World, Bradley takes on the role of curious investigator rather than claiming to have all the answers.

He approaches each subject with an open mind, speaking to people who believe they have encountered something extraordinary while remaining cautious about accepting claims without evidence.

That balance is central to the appeal of the programme.

The presenter has also spoken about how fascinating he found some of the people and evidence encountered during filming, particularly those involved in the Atlantis investigation.

Bradley Walsh: Out of This World – is tonight’s Atlantis mystery worth watching?

For viewers fascinated by unexplained mysteries, ancient history and the possibility of life beyond Earth, Bradley Walsh: Out of This World offers an entertaining combination of investigation, travel and factual storytelling.

Tonight’s Atlantis episode is particularly intriguing, taking Bradley from Gibraltar to the Spanish coast in search of clues about a civilisation that may have disappeared beneath the waves thousands of years ago.

Whether viewers are convinced by the theories or remain firmly sceptical, the programme offers an opportunity to explore the evidence and consider some fascinating historical questions.

Bradley’s enthusiasm and trademark humour also ensure that the journey is never too serious.

Bradley Walsh: Out of This World airs tonight at 9pm on Sky HISTORY, with Bradley investigating the mystery of Atlantis and following ancient clues along the Spanish coast.
